O-02.m: On the aesthetics of sweet desserts.

O-04.m: Chuseok special: answering awkward questions from relatives like a contemporary artist.

O-05.m: A playlist that smells like autumn.

O-07.m: J and G review things they bought recently.

O-08.m: How the eee team divides the work.

K-01.m: Diaspora means living away from home. In art, it becomes a question of identity: where do I belong?

K-02.m: For Agamben, being contemporary means being out of step with your time. Doubt lets you see the present clearly.

K-03.m: Benjamin's aura is not a quality of the object but a way of experiencing it, and it changed in the age of reproduction.

K-04.m: Duchamp's urinal, Fountain, was a readymade that shook the very rules of what counts as art.

K-05.m: Pop art borrows familiar mass-culture images to make the system of consumption and desire behind them strange.

K-06.m: The sublime is the fear and fascination we feel when our senses fail before something vast.

K-07.m: Minimalism strips away emotion and story so we see form, material and space themselves.

K-08.m: The parergon, from Kant to Derrida: what sits outside a work, like a frame, and makes it read as a work.

K-09.m: The horror film The Backrooms hides the grammar of modern art: dépaysement and cubism.

K-10.m: Korean abstraction took its own path, holding post-war feeling, nature and traces of material and body.

K-11.m: Meet the art handlers who pack, ship, install and take down works after a show ends.

K-12.m: Feel like doing the opposite of what a work asks? Roland Barthes on whether we must follow the artist's intent.

K-13.m: Hirsch says follow the artist's intent; Shusterman says everyday responses count as interpretation too.

K-14.m: Must art be beautiful? Rosenkranz's aesthetics of ugliness and art that shows the uncomfortable.

K-15.m: The fourth wall: the invisible wall between stage and audience, and the moments that break it.

K-16.m: Brecht made the familiar strange so audiences would see the social causes behind a tragedy.

K-17.m: In conceptual art, like Kosuth's three chairs, the idea and structure become the work itself.

K-18.m: Joseph Beuys's social sculpture: thought, speech, debate and politics as creative acts that shape society.

K-19.m: Frieze, now a global art fair, began as a small contemporary art magazine made by two friends.

K-20.m: How the makers of frieze magazine launched a fair in London in 2003, with film, talks and performance.

K-21.m: Art was once touched in temples and altars. When did it become something we keep our distance from?

K-22.m: Were frames always part of the painting? A history of frames and who chooses them.

K-23.m: Wall texts are written by curators, then edited, checked and designed before they reach the gallery.

K-24.m: An artwork's price mixes the artist's fame, market attention and someone's judgment.

K-25.m: Curators research and choose the works in a show, and decide the order we meet them in.

K-26.m: Why are endlessly reproducible photos sold in limited numbers? The edition system explained.

F-01.m: EEE Fight Club, where we argue over controversial art. Cattelan's banana: artist or con man?

F-02.m: Jackson Pollock dripped and poured paint. Hype, or a master who changed art?

F-03.m: Tracey Emin showed her own bed. Honest, or just uncomfortable?

F-04.m: Cho Young-nam left the painting to assistants. A fake artist?

F-05.m: Man Ray destroyed his work, then made it again. What is an original?

F-06.m: Brancusi's bird doesn't look like a bird. How do we judge it?

F-07.m: Banksy struck at the art market. Can the system change?

F-08.m: Chuseok special: until what age is it fine to get holiday pocket money?

F-09.m: The audience freely followed the artist's instructions. Can violence inside a work be justified?

F-10.m: In an age that praised nude goddesses, why was Olympia so attacked?

F-11.m: If only one artist may use a certain black, is that monopoly fair?

F-12.m: Santiago Sierra tattooed others' bodies to expose exploitation. Can it be justified?

F-13.m: Yayoi Kusama sold works for $2. Artistic resistance, or clever PR?

F-14.m: Running Fence took three and a half years and came down in two weeks. What was it worth?
